clue.text: Catch pitiful vehicle with ticket in end

indicators.note: the words before it are placed inside the word that follows, as if held within it

parts.note: to die is to come to an end
a pitiful sight is a sad one
a van is a delivery vehicle
a tag or label, like a price ticket

explanation.surface: Someone stuck with a miserable car and a parking ticket at the end of the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Catch' looks like a verb, but it is the noun for a hidden snag; 'end' is the verb to die.
explanation.definitionFit: A catch is a hidden snag or drawback, so it is a noun synonym for a handicap or weakness.

clue.text: New rule up on red gate in part of airport

indicators.note: something new has been made afresh, so the following letters are rebuilt in another order

parts.note: fifteen letters of fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: A fresh regulation has been posted on a red-painted gate somewhere in a terminal.
explanation.definitionFit: Passengers wait in this hall before boarding, making it one section of an airport terminal building.

clue.text: Poor judge after support

parts.note: to second a motion is to support it
to rate something is to judge its worth

explanation.surface: A weak judge only rules after getting someone's backing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' places the judge word behind the support word.
explanation.definitionFit: Something second-rate is of inferior quality, so it matches poor as an adjective of low standard.

clue.text: Staff upset about extremes of erratic colour scheme

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece surrounds the other
in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a rod is a staff or stick

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its outermost letters, first and last

parts.note: first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: Staff are upset by a decorator's erratic choice of colours.
explanation.definitionFit: Decor is the overall style of furnishing and painting a room, which includes its chosen palette of shades.

clue.text: Partnerships completely ruined in case

parts.note: all the way means completely

indicators.note: something ruined is wrecked, so the words after it are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, the fodder

explanation.surface: Business partnerships were totally wrecked in a legal case.
explanation.definitionFit: Alliances are unions formed between parties for mutual benefit, a plural noun for joint ventures or associations.

clue.text: Run temperature? Nonsense

parts.note: T is the standard abbreviation for temperature
rot means rubbish or nonsense

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether to go for a run with a fever and is told not to be silly.
explanation.definitionFit: To trot is to move at a gentle jogging pace, a light kind of running.

clue.text: French author, fantastic but vague, falters

indicators.note: fantastic suggests something wildly imagined, so these letters are reshaped into a new form

parts.note: fifteen letters of fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: A critic's verdict on a writer: brilliant, yet woolly, and his prose stumbles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fantastic' looks like praise of the author, but it signals the rearrangement of the next three words.
explanation.definitionFit: Gustave Flaubert was the nineteenth-century novelist from Normandy who wrote Madame Bovary.

clue.text: Mass to occupy top American college area

indicators.note: to occupy a place is to sit inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a cap is a top or lid
M is the abbreviation for mass
US is short for American

explanation.surface: Crowds of people take over a leading American university's grounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A campus is the grounds and buildings of a university or college, the site where it stands.

clue.text: Look at rent making small hole

parts.note: to eye something is to look at it
to let a property is to rent it out

explanation.surface: Inspecting a tear in fabric that has produced a tiny gap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rent' looks like a tear, which suits a hole, but it means to hire out.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyelet is a little reinforced opening in cloth or leather for a lace or cord to pass through.

clue.text: Dreams, short of rations, about jelly

indicators.note: short of means lacking, so the named word is taken away from the longer one

parts.note: aspirations are hopes or dreams
taken as written, the part removed
C stands for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: Hungry people dream of food when their rations run low, perhaps even of jelly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short of rations' reads as hunger, but rations is a whole word taken out of the dreams word. C stands for circa.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspic is a savoury gelatine made from meat stock, used to set cold dishes, so it is a kind of jelly.

clue.text: Cruelly inexperienced, losing wicket, undone initially by cunning

indicators.note: losing something means it is dropped from the word in question

parts.note: callow means young and inexperienced
W is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for wicket

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word beside it

parts.note: first letter of the word
sly means cunning

explanation.surface: A green cricketer loses his wicket, beaten by a crafty bowler, and is treated harshly.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a batter who is out loses his wicket; scorecards mark it W.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting callously means acting with hard-hearted indifference to others' suffering, which is cruel behaviour.

clue.text: Artist, joined by number in Italian city, left without natural explanation

indicators.note: in places the preceding pieces inside the city named after it

parts.note: Parma is a city in northern Italy
RA, Royal Academician, a crossword artist
No. is the abbreviation for number
L is short for left

explanation.surface: A painter teams up with a companion in an Italian city and then departs.
explanation.walkthrough: RA, a Royal Academician, is the usual crossword artist; 'left' looks like departing but is the direction letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Paranormal events lie beyond the reach of scientific understanding, which is to say they cannot be accounted for by nature.

clue.text: Follow story from speaker

indicators.note: coming from a speaker means the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: a tale is a story

explanation.surface: Track down the source of a rumour by following what someone said.
explanation.definitionFit: To tail someone is to shadow them closely without being seen, as a detective does.

clue.text: Wilful leader's weight about right? Good

parts.note: a head is a leader, with the possessive s

indicators.note: about means around, so the weight word wraps around the next piece

parts.note: a ton is a unit of weight
R is short for right
G is short for good

explanation.surface: A stubborn boss asks whether his heavy influence is right and is told it is good.
explanation.definitionFit: A headstrong person is obstinate and determined to have their own way, which is what wilful describes.

clue.text: Engineers in group agreed

indicators.note: in places the first piece inside the second

parts.note: a squad is a group or team
RE, the Royal Engineers of the British Army

explanation.surface: A team of engineers reached consensus.
explanation.definitionFit: When accounts are squared they tally, and to square with something is to fit or be consistent with it.

clue.text: Sporting event strangely not held outside California

indicators.note: outside means the rearranged letters surround the state abbreviation
strangely means in an odd way, so the following words are oddly rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, the fodder
CA is the postal abbreviation for California

explanation.surface: An athletics meet surprisingly not staged outside California.
explanation.definitionFit: The decathlon is an athletics contest of ten track and field disciplines, contested at the Olympics.

clue.text: Mild chapter, part lacking energy

parts.note: C is short for chapter

indicators.note: lacking means without, so a letter is removed from the word before it

parts.note: an element is a component part
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A gentle chapter, one section of a book that has no vigour.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the first E of ELEMENT goes, leaving LEMENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Clement weather is pleasantly temperate, and a clement judge is merciful, both gentle senses of the adjective.

clue.text: One inclined to question power in sect not usually in charge

indicators.note: in places the first letter inside the rearranged word
not in the usual way means the word's letters appear in an unusual order

parts.note: taken as written, the fodder
P is the physics symbol for power
i/c is the abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: A doubter within a religious group where authority is seldom held by one person.
explanation.definitionFit: A sceptic habitually doubts claims and accepted beliefs, so they are a person disposed to query things.

clue.text: Bits of satire I'd cite that aren't even accurate

indicators.note: only some bits are kept, namely those in the positions the clue goes on to describe
positions that are not even are the odd ones, first, third, fifth and so on

parts.note: the first, third, fifth letters and so on

explanation.surface: Fragments of satire I'd quote are not fair or balanced, says a critic who prizes precision.
explanation.definitionFit: Strict can mean exact or precise in interpretation, as in a strict translation that is faithful to the original.

clue.text: Landed in south, confused

parts.note: S is short for south
addled means muddled or confused

explanation.surface: A traveller touches down in the south, feeling disoriented.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Landed' looks like arriving by plane, but it is the sense of being burdened with something.
explanation.definitionFit: To be landed with a task is to be lumbered or burdened with it, the same as being saddled with it.

clue.text: Youngster put up with tacky stuff in order

indicators.note: in a down clue, put up means placed upward, so the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: a kid is a youngster
tat is cheap, tasteless goods

explanation.surface: A child has had to tolerate cheap junk kept neatly arranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A diktat is a decree imposed by an authority without consent, a harsh command or order.

clue.text: Piece on board for bird

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a chess piece, also called a castle
second meaning: a black crow that nests in colonies

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests swapping a game piece for a bird; the two are separate meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the castle-shaped chess man and a gregarious crow-family species found across Europe.

clue.text: Jump around front of stage with crowd captivated by famous people

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the jump word wraps the next letter

parts.note: to start is to jump with surprise

indicators.note: the front of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of the word
a ruck is a dense crowd or scrum

explanation.surface: Fans leap about near the stage, a crowd enthralled by celebrities.
explanation.walkthrough: A ruck is a tightly packed crowd, a word also used for a rugby scrum-like tussle.
explanation.definitionFit: Being starstruck means being dazzled and awed by celebrities, so it describes someone held spellbound by the well known.

clue.text: Rector's first love? University, endlessly splendid

indicators.note: endlessly means without its end, so the last letter is dropped
first points to the opening letter of the word it is attached to

parts.note: first letter of the word
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
Yale is an American Ivy League university

explanation.surface: A clergyman's first love is a university he considers magnificent.
explanation.definitionFit: Royal can mean magnificent or fit for a king, as in a royal welcome, so it matches splendid.

clue.text: Produced signal to stop following bishop

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the signal is placed behind the churchman's letter

parts.note: B is the chess notation for bishop
a red light tells traffic to halt

explanation.surface: A bishop, following behind, is waved down by a traffic light.
explanation.walkthrough: In chess notation B stands for bishop, a common crossword abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Animals that are bred have been raised or reared, so the past participle means produced as offspring.

clue.text: Essentially needing a bit of money before meeting

parts.note: a cent is a small coin
a rally is a mass meeting

explanation.surface: Fundamentally, it takes some cash to hold a gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Before' puts the money in front of the meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: Centrally means at the core or heart of a matter, so it works as an adverb for fundamentally or basically.

clue.text: Last letter from troublesome gangster

indicators.note: from means taken out of the words that follow, which hold the answer within them

parts.note: the letters run across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: A final message received from a violent mobster.
explanation.definitionFit: Omega is the twenty-fourth and final character of the Greek alphabet, hence the closing one.

clue.text: Influential figure in field, mostly dull and undemanding

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a lea is a meadow or field, a poetic word
dingy means drab and dull
light reading is undemanding

explanation.surface: A prominent person in some discipline turns out to be largely boring and easygoing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In field' reads as 'in their field of work', but field is the meadow word.
explanation.definitionFit: A leading light is a prominent and respected member of a group who guides others, an idiom for an important person.
